title: The Web’s Secret: How Your Browser Talks

scenes.line2: when you load a web page?
scenes.say: Ever wonder what your browser actually does when you hit Enter on a link? Let's break down the magic behind every page load.

scenes.label: DNS
scenes.sub: Translates a website name to an IP address.
scenes.say: First, the browser asks DNS to turn the site name into a real internet address.
Next, your browser builds a connection, locks it down with encryption, and finally sends an HTTP request.

scenes.title: Server replies
scenes.say: The server answers with your page, sets cookies for tracking, and tells the browser how to cache it.
Cookies and tokens help remember who you are. Cookies are sent automatically, while tokens are more flexible and scalable.

scenes.question: Does TLS only protect passwords?
scenes.right: No, TLS encrypts all data between browser and server, not just passwords.
scenes.say: A common trap: TLS doesn't just hide passwords. It protects every bit of data sent between your browser and the server.
